Quantify ligand incorporation via XPS (N 1s shifts), UV–vis (Soret/Q-band shifts), and Zn coordination signatures. This series is the primary lever to shift E_onset,app and ORR kinetics (Asset 1 link via half-wave potential as a quantitative descriptor).

Step 2 — Mandatory Pillar (1): Quantitative energy-level alignment + microkinetic ORR model
2.1 Measure interfacial energetics under dark and illumination:
- UPS (work function, valence onset) and inverse photoemission / calibrated electron affinity estimates where possible for ZnPor-COF and carbon.
- KPFM mapping across cross-sections (or surface after layer-by-layer build) to obtain local contact potential difference (CPD). Do this in controlled atmosphere with tunable O2 partial pressure (0–1 atm) and humidity (0–50% RH).
- Kelvin probe (macroscopic) vs pO2 to capture oxygen-induced work-function shifts and adsorption-induced dipoles.
2.2 Determine illuminated E_Fn at the perovskite electron-contact side:
- Use surface photovoltage (SPV) + KPFM under 1-sun equivalent visible illumination to extract the quasi-Fermi level splitting at the top electron-contact surface (C60/BCP/PCP) in inert vs O2.
- Cross-check with absolute PLQY-derived QFLS of completed stacks (perovskite + ETL + PCP) to anchor E_Fn changes.
2.3 ORR electrochemical descriptors on the actual stacks:
- Three-electrode microcell using carbon/(ZnPor-COF) as working electrode; match humidity to PSC-relevant conditions (dry to low-moisture, aligning with quasi-solid-state constraints highlighted in Asset 1).
- Measure ORR polarization curves, half-wave potential (E1/2), Tafel slopes, and selectivity to H2O2 via RRDE (ring detection) where feasible; otherwise use rotating disk + colorimetric peroxide assays with strict calibration.
2.4 Microkinetic model coupling energetics to H2O2 yield (Asset 2 linkage):
- Use a two-pathway scheme: 4e− ORR to OH−/H2O and 2e− ORR to H2O2, with rate constants k2(E, aO2, awater) and k4(E, aO2, awater). Parameterize k2/k4 from RRDE selectivity and Tafel slopes.
- Include partitioning/transport of H2O2 through COF as a 1D diffusion-reaction term: ∂c/∂t = D_eff∂²c/∂x² − k_decay c, where D_eff and k_decay depend on sulfonation/water uptake.
- Output prediction: H2O2 activity at the perovskite-side boundary a_H2O2(x=0) vs (E_Fn,illum, pO2, RH, ligand). Define a quantitative success threshold: ≥10× reduction in a_H2O2(x=0) relative to carbon-only control at matched pO2/RH.

Step 3 — Mandatory Pillar (2): Deconvolute NIR effects; rule out singlet oxygen (1O2)
3.1 Optical/thermal controls (causal isolation):
- NIR gating: 808–850 nm LED, 10–30 mW cm−2, duty-cycled (e.g., 10%–50%) with temperature rise constrained to <2 °C.
- Temperature-matched dark controls: resistive microheater or IR heater to replicate the exact temperature profile without photons.
- Photon-flux matched visible controls: visible LED adjusted to deposit equal absorbed power in carbon/COF but not excite ZnPor triplets equivalently (confirmed by absorption spectra), to separate photothermal vs photochemical effects.
3.2 Direct 1O2 detection with immobilized probes and EPR:
- Immobilize SOSG or DPBF in an oxygen-permeable, perovskite-inert polymer layer positioned on the air-side (carbon/ZnPor-COF side) to avoid probe diffusion to perovskite.
- Perform EPR spin trapping with TEMP to detect TEMPO formation under NIR; compare (i) ZnPor-COF with each axial ligand, (ii) carbon-only, (iii) ZnPor-COF + physical 1O2 quencher barrier (e.g., immobilized DABCO derivative or HALS additive in a thin overlayer).
- Acceptance criterion: NIR-on condition increases ORR current/lowers interfacial peroxide signal while 1O2 signal remains unchanged (≤10% change) or is reduced with quencher without loss of ORR benefit.
3.3 Confirm NIR changes ORR kinetics at fixed overpotential (not via increased η):
- Measure ORR current at fixed applied potentials (or fixed electrode potential vs reference) with NIR on/off at constant temperature; extract Δj and infer Δj0.

Step 4 — GOx integration (mandated chain completion) as a calibrated H2O2 generator reference
4.1 Build a separate GOx test fixture (no perovskite) to isolate peroxide flux and Fenton gating:
- Architecture: carbon/(ZnPor-COF variants)/PCP on inert substrate; adjacent hydrogel layer containing GOx + glucose (controlled rate of H2O2 generation).
- Quantify generated H2O2 flux using microelectrode/SECM and colorimetric assays; vary COF sulfonation and thickness.
4.2 Fenton suppression benchmark under controlled Fe contamination (Assets 3–4 linkage):
- Add Fe2+/Fe3+ (ppb–ppm) to the GOx hydrogel; measure ·OH via EPR (DMPO-·OH) and/or terephthalic acid fluorescence (with immobilization).
- Compare stacks with/without PCP; extract an inhibition factor for ·OH generation vs Fe dose. Acceptance criterion: ≥90% suppression of ·OH across 0.1–10 ppm Fe under fixed H2O2 flux.

Step 5 — Operando ROS mapping in PSC-relevant stacks
5.1 Spatially resolved peroxide mapping:
- SECM in humidity-controlled chamber to map local H2O2 near the carbon/ZnPor-COF surface vs near the perovskite-adjacent side (using a laminated proxy stack if direct access is limited).
- Polymer-bound peroxide fluorescent probes confined to the air-side; verify no probe migration by ToF-SIMS tagging.
5.2 Hydroxyl radical and superoxide assays near perovskite interface:
- EPR on encapsulated mini-stacks with spin traps localized at the perovskite-adjacent side (immobilized trap in an interlayer) to avoid sampling artifacts.

Step 6 — Device physics endpoints and ROS-coupled rate-law validation (replace “apoptosis”)
6.1 Device performance under controlled O2/RH/light (ISOS-O and ISOS-L variants): track PCE, Voc, Jsc, FF; extract T80 and Voc retention.
6.2 Quantify non-radiative recombination and defect growth:
- Absolute PLQY/QFLS before/after stress; transient photovoltage/photocurrent; impedance spectroscopy for recombination resistance changes under O2.
- Trap density evolution via thermal admittance spectroscopy and/or SCLC in dedicated electron-only devices.
6.3 Ion migration markers:
- Hysteresis index vs stress time; transient ion drift signatures (e.g., bias-assisted capacitance transients).
6.4 Rate-law coupling to measured ROS:
- Fit degradation rate (e.g., d(Voc)/dt or d(trap density)/dt) to measured a_H2O2(x=0), ·OH EPR intensity, and 1O2 signals under each condition (ligand, sulfonation, NIR controls, Fe contamination). Success is a model-consistent causal chain: reduced peroxide activity at the perovskite-side + suppressed ·OH correlates with slower Voc-deficit growth.

Step 7 — Zinc-air battery cathode transfer validation (Asset 1 linkage)
7.1 Assemble quasi-solid-state zinc-air battery cathodes using the same ZnPor-COF/carbon (with ligand series) and measure ORR half-wave potential and power density vs carbon-only.
7.2 Use E1/2 improvement and moisture-dependence as an orthogonal confirmation that the interphase provides meaningful ORR kinetics in low-moisture environments, consistent with the PSC air-electrode regime.

Go/No-Go milestones (explicit):
M1 Energetics: obtain E_Fn,illum(contact) and E_onset,app(ZnPor-COF) on a common vacuum-referenced scale; demonstrate ≥150 mV separation under operating conditions.
M2 NIR causality: at temperature-matched conditions, NIR increases ORR rate/selectivity metrics without increasing 1O2 (TEMP/SOSG/DPBF) and without increasing perovskite-side ROS.
M3 Transport: demonstrate ≥10× lower perovskite-side peroxide activity with optimized sulfonation/thickness.
M4 Fenton gate: demonstrate ≥90% suppression of ·OH with PCP under GOx-generated H2O2 and ppm Fe.
M5 Device stability: demonstrate statistically significant improvement in T80 and Voc retention under ISOS-O with the full interphase vs controls (carbon-only, ZnPor-COF only, PCP only).
Feasibility: Energy-level alignment feasibility: UPS/KPFM/SPV are standard, quantitative tools for mapping work function and illumination-induced potential changes; coupling these to a microkinetic ORR model directly answers the reviewer’s concern that “outside the quasi-Fermi level” was underdefined. Using a single reference framework (vacuum level) and reporting explicit thresholds (≥150 mV separation; ≥10× reduction in a_H2O2 at the perovskite boundary) converts the concept into falsifiable criteria.

NIR deconvolution feasibility and 1O2 risk management: The reviewer-cited failure mode (porphyrin triplet-sensitized 1O2) is explicitly addressed with orthogonal detection (immobilized SOSG/DPBF and TEMP/TEMPO EPR) and with temperature-matched and photon-flux matched controls to separate photothermal and photochemical effects. If 1O2 is detected, the plan includes a compatible mitigation (immobilized quencher overlayer) and a decision gate that requires maintaining ORR benefit without elevating 1O2.

Peroxide transport/selectivity feasibility: Sulfonation-dependent water uptake and D_eff can be quantified (QCM-D/porosimetry/SECM), enabling a transport-informed optimization rather than an assumption. The 1D diffusion-reaction model is deliberately minimal yet sufficient to demonstrate whether peroxide activity at the perovskite-side boundary decreases, which is the only transport outcome that matters for stability.

GOx integration (mandated chain coherence): GOx is added not as a PSC component but as a calibrated H2O2 source in a separate fixture to validate peroxide flux handling and PCP’s Fe/Fenton suppression with controlled inputs—mirroring Assets 3–4 where H2O2 availability governs downstream radical chemistry. This satisfies the required concept chain (H2O2 ↔ ORR ↔ Fenton) while preventing biological irrelevancies from contaminating PSC interpretation.

Relevance and endpoints: “Apoptosis” is replaced with PSC-native, quantifiable failure metrics (Voc-deficit growth, trap density increase, ion-migration signatures) and explicitly linked to ROS observables through rate-law fitting. This creates a causally testable chain from ORR energetics/kinetics → H2O2 activity → (Fe-gated) ·OH formation → electronic/ionic degradation signatures.

Transfer validation logic (zinc-air linkage): Using half-wave potential (E1/2) and QSS zinc-air battery power density as orthogonal measures (Assets 1–2) validates that the same ZnPor-COF/carbon chemistry provides meaningful ORR competence in low-moisture regimes. This reduces risk that the interphase is merely a passive barrier and substantiates its intended electrocatalytic role without introducing noble metals or Fenton-active centers.
final_critique: The proposal is unusually strong on operational definitions, falsifiable milestones, and control logic. The main technical weaknesses are (i) the claimed ≥150 mV “E_Fn,illum(contact) vs E_onset,app” separation is not yet convincingly measurable on a single absolute scale under identical chemical potentials: KPFM/UPS/SPV provide work functions and photovoltages, but mapping these to an electrochemical ORR onset in humid O2 without a rigorously defined interfacial reference state (water activity, local pH, double-layer potential, carbon doping/adsorbates) risks systematic offsets larger than the 150 mV threshold; (ii) the microkinetic/transport model is still underconstrained—selectivity and Tafel data alone will not uniquely identify k2/k4 and H2O2 boundary activity without independent calibration of local water content, O2 permeability, and potential distribution through the COF; (iii) the NIR mechanism as written (“triplets accelerate back-electron transfer / interfacial charge-exchange with O2 increasing j0 at fixed η”) is plausible but ambiguous—triplet–O2 interactions commonly *increase* 1O2 unless explicitly quenched, so the plan needs a clearer mechanistic discriminant (e.g., outer-sphere ET vs energy transfer) tied to measurable spectroscopic signatures; (iv) PCP deposition feasibility on/near perovskite stacks is a risk: even ‘pre-integration’ deposition on ETL can alter ETL energetics, introduce dipoles, and add ionic functionalities affecting hysteresis—this could confound attribution to ROS suppression unless additional electrical controls (dark JV, electron-only mobility/contact resistance) are built in. Overall, deductions are for metrology traceability at the ORR/energetics interface and parameter identifiability, not for lack of rigor.
hypothesis_summary: A redox-buffering interphase with NIR-gated oxygen management suppresses perovskite degradation by shifting oxygen reduction away from the perovskite, minimizing peroxide activity, and blocking Fenton chemistry.

original_chain: Utilization ratio -> bmFeSAC -> Schwarz P surface -> Electrocatalytic activity -> Amorphous isoreticular metal organic framework-3 (aIRMOF-3)
proposal_content:
Hypothesis: A perovskite-compatible, electronically benign bicontinuous passivation manifold can be realized by combining: (i) an ultrathin (3–6 nm) *metal-free* aminated coordination glass (aIRMOF-3 chemistry translated into a Zn-free, carboxylate-free, dipole-controlled network) that immobilizes undercoordinated Pb–(I/Br) surface species and pins halide-vacancy migration; (ii) a *Schwarz P–class* (P-surface–targeted) bicontinuous minimal-surface morphology that increases interfacial area and homogenizes interfacial electric-field/ionic-flux distributions; and (iii) wall-confined Fe–N4 single-atom redox centers positioned in the *gas-accessible* internal walls but *energetically and kinetically gated* to avoid acting as recombination sites.

Mechanistic resolution of reviewer risks:
1) **Composition control / ionic contamination:** Replace Zn2+/carboxylate motifs with a neutral, coordinatively saturated, aminated “coordination-glass analogue” built from (a) multidentate amines/ureas/guanidiniums (Lewis bases for Pb2+), (b) non-ionic covalent crosslinking (thiol–ene or SPAAC click), and (c) optional zwitterion buffering groups to tune interfacial dipole to ~0. This maintains the aIRMOF-3 *functional logic* (high-density donor sites + amorphous conformality) while avoiding Zn2+ leaching, carboxylate-driven interfacial dipoles, and photochemical metal–ligand rearrangements.
2) **Curvature suppresses ionic hot spots (quantified):** In perovskites, mobile halide vacancies and ionic defects drift under local fields and accumulate at transport interfaces, accelerating field-assisted defect formation and interfacial recombination. A Schwarz P–class bicontinuous interface imposes negative Gaussian curvature and spatially distributed surface normals. Under a coupled Poisson–Nernst–Planck (PNP) model using realistic dielectric contrast (εperovskite ~ 20–30; εorganic ~ 3–5), this geometry reduces peak interfacial electric-field magnitude and the variance of the normal field component En at the perovskite contact, lowering the steady-state ionic concentration polarization (Δc/c0) and the accumulation time constant (τacc) relative to a flat film at identical thickness and applied bias. This provides a *predictive* reduction in experimentally observable KPFM potential pile-up and bias-stress impedance signatures.
3) **Fe–N4 ROS sink without halide oxidation or recombination:** Fe–N4 sites are introduced with (a) a ligand field designed to place Fe(III/II) redox below halide-oxidation thresholds and (b) an ultrathin tunneling/kinetic barrier that permits ROS interception (requiring only local electron availability) but suppresses electronic back-transfer into perovskite bands. The key is to ensure: (i) Fe redox levels are off-resonant from perovskite band edges at operating quasi-Fermi-level splitting, (ii) no additional subgap absorption is introduced, and (iii) carrier recombination metrics (PLQY at 1-sun carrier density, ideality factor, subgap EQE) do not degrade. If these quantitative gates are met, the Fe–N4 centers operate as a selective redox sink for superoxide/peroxide intermediates in oxygen-containing environments, reducing oxygen-driven interfacial chemistry without becoming a recombination-active manifold.

Net expected outcome: higher Voc/FF through reduced interfacial nonradiative recombination and reduced ionic accumulation, plus improved oxygen/light/heat operational stability through ROS interception—achieved without the series-resistance penalty of insulating crystalline MOFs, because the manifold is ultrathin, bicontinuous, and electronically tuned by dipole control and barrier-gated redox centers.
Plan: A. Baseline system and controls (unchanged core concept, expanded controls to satisfy recombination-risk separation)
A1. Device baseline (interface-limited): (FA0.85Cs0.15)Pb(I0.85Br0.15)3 in p–i–n: ITO/2PACz (or NiOx)/Perovskite/Interlayer/C60/BCP/Ag. Target perovskite thickness 450–650 nm; C60 15–25 nm.
A2. Control matrix (expanded):
- C0: no interlayer.
- C1: aminated coordination glass only (flat, 3–6 nm; no bicontinuity; no Fe).
- C2: bicontinuous P-surface–targeted manifold without Fe (topology only).
- C3: Fe–N4 in flat glass (chemistry only).
- C4: full manifold (glass + P-surface topology + wall-confined Fe–N4).
- C5 (mandatory recombination-risk control): Fe–N4 present but electronically insulated via a defined tunneling spacer (0.8–1.2 nm aliphatic/fluorinated barrier) between Fe–N4 and the electronically coupled wall; ROS access maintained but electronic coupling reduced.
- C6 (dipole control): identical to C4 but with zwitterion-buffered vs non-buffered glass to quantify band alignment sensitivity.

B. Mandatory Gate 3 (Process-compatibility): perovskite-inert route to create bicontinuity without plasma
B1. Replace plasma domain removal with **orthogonal solvent extraction** or **photocleavable sacrificial block**.
- Preferred route: PS-b-PEO (or PI-b-PEO) with PEO as sacrificial domain; crosslink the PS (or PI) domain via UV thiol–ene using inert thiols; extract PEO using anhydrous ethanol or acetonitrile (validated perovskite-safe) at room temperature.
- Alternative route (if extraction insufficient): BCP with **o-nitrobenzyl** photocleavable sidechains in sacrificial block; after crosslinking the matrix block, cleave sacrificial block under 365–405 nm low-fluence (<10 mW cm−2) in N2; rinse with orthogonal solvent.
B2. Demonstration on perovskite films (gate criteria):
- Processing sequence on perovskite/2PACz stacks without C60.
- Pass criteria (all must hold):
  (i) XRD: no new PbI2 peak growth beyond +2% relative integrated intensity vs untreated;
  (ii) UV–Vis: ΔAbs(500–800 nm) < 1% and no new tailing;
  (iii) XPS/ToF-SIMS: no measurable halide depletion at top 20 nm (I/Pb ratio change <5%; Br/Pb <5%); no new oxidized iodine signature above noise;
  (iv) PL (steady-state) intensity on perovskite does not drop >10% vs solvent-only control.
- Go/no-go: if any fail, switch to a “non-etched” bicontinuity route (Section B4 contingency).
B3. Targeted P-surface formation in confined film:
- Use solvent-vapor annealing (SVA) with controlled vapor activity (toluene/THF blends) to steer toward P-surface–class bicontinuity (distinguished from gyroid by GISAXS peak positions and relative intensities).
- Film thickness 20 ± 5 nm to remain optically thin and compatible with C60 conformality.
B4. Contingency if true P-surface is not reproducible: adopt gyroid bicontinuous phase but preserve the *negative Gaussian curvature distribution* criterion by selecting a bicontinuous morphology with similar curvature statistics (quantified from tomography). The mechanistic tests (Gate 2) remain geometry-driven; proceed only if modeled and measured ionic-accumulation reduction is achieved.

C. Glass interlayer redesign (addresses Zn/carboxylate/dipole risk while preserving “aIRMOF-3 amorphous framework” logic)
C1. Composition: a neutral covalent network with dense Lewis-base motifs.
- Monomers: multifunctional amines (e.g., tris(2-aminoethyl)amine derivatives), urea/thiourea motifs (for Pb2+ coordination), optional guanidinium-like H-bond donors (for halide-vacancy stabilization).
- Crosslinking: SPAAC (azide–DBCO) or thiol–ene, chosen to avoid acidic/byproduct ions.
- Dipole tuning: incorporate zwitterionic sulfobetaine units at 5–15 mol% to neutralize net dipole and stabilize work function.
C2. Deposition: solvent-orthogonal sequential vapor/solution steps.
- Step 1: deposit 0.5–1.5 nm primer SAM (already compatible: 2PACz underlayer; on top surface use an ultrathin inert “landing” layer such as HMDS-like silazane or fluorinated alkylsilane if needed).
- Step 2: spin-coat or vapor-deliver monomers from dry, nonpolar/weakly polar solvents (anisole, chlorobenzene, or dry IPA if validated) with total thickness 3–6 nm.
- Step 3: room-temperature crosslink (UV 365–405 nm, low dose, inert atmosphere) to lock amorphous network.
C3. Pb2+/halide-vacancy binding verification (before topology integration):
- XPS core-level shifts (Pb 4f, I 3d, N 1s) consistent with Pb–N coordination;
- 2D solid-state NMR on witness films (optional);
- Reduced trap density via SCLC and increased PLQY on perovskite/glass vs perovskite bare.

D. Mandatory Gate 1 (Band/redox alignment): compute then measure; prohibit device integration until passed
D1. Computation (pre-screen):
- DFT/cluster calculations for Fe–N4 embedded in the wall ligand environment + dielectric embedding to estimate Fe(III/II) redox and frontier-state energies; compute expected work function shifts from glass composition (with and without zwitterions).
D2. Measurements on model stacks (ITO/interlayer/C60 and perovskite/interlayer/C60):
- UPS/IPES: determine interlayer-induced work-function (WF) and band-edge alignment; Kelvin probe mapping for spatial uniformity (<30 mV RMS variation).
- Under illumination (1 sun equivalent carrier density in perovskite): Kelvin probe / surface photovoltage to ensure no adverse interfacial dipole-induced barrier.
- Electrochemical redox of Fe–N4 in solid state: thin-film spectroelectrochemistry on ITO/interlayer in dry O2/N2 with a non-aqueous electrolyte (or redox mediator) to extract effective Fe(III/II) potential; corroborate with in situ XPS (Fe 2p shifts) vs applied bias.
D3. Pass criteria (all required, go/no-go):
- Optical: no new subgap absorption; specifically ΔEQE (below bandgap) < 1×10−4 absolute and no additional absorption tail in PDS.
- Photophysics: PLQY of perovskite/interlayer/C60 at 1-sun-equivalent carrier density not reduced by >10% vs C0; TRPL fast component not shortened.
- Energetics: interlayer WF shift magnitude |ΔWF| ≤ 0.15 eV unless it improves electron extraction without reducing Voc in quasi-steady-state PL; Fe redox must not be placed within ±0.2 eV of perovskite quasi-Fermi levels under operation (empirically assessed by matching to SPV/Kelvin under light).
- If fails: implement C5-style insulation barrier or alter ligand field (electron-withdrawing substituents) to move Fe redox away; if still fails, drop Fe and proceed with topology+glass only (C2+C1 path).

E. P-surface manifold fabrication (perovskite-safe)
E1. Build sequence:
1) Perovskite deposition + anneal.
2) Glass formation (3–6 nm).
3) BCP coating (15–25 nm) + SVA to achieve bicontinuity.
4) Crosslink matrix block.
5) Remove sacrificial block by orthogonal extraction / photocleavage (Gate 3 already qualified).
6) Optional: coat internal walls with a 0.5–1.0 nm “electronic spacer” (alkyl/fluoroalkyl or wide-gap siloxane) to tune coupling (used for C5 and as knob for C4).
E2. Topology validation (quantitative):
- GISAXS: fit to P-surface–class structure factor; accept if long-range periodicity with domain spacing 10–30 nm and low disorder parameter.
- Cross-sectional tomography (FIB-SEM with low-dose or soft X-ray tomography): quantify connectivity and curvature statistics; require percolation in-plane and through-thickness.

F. Fe–N4 wall-confined installation (site placement + benignity)
F1. Ligand anchoring exclusively on internal walls:
- Introduce tethered tetra-aza macrocycle precursors (porphyrinoid or cyclam-like) via click coupling to wall functional handles (azide/alkyne).
- Control ligand areal density: 0.1–1.0 sites nm−2 (screened).
F2. Metalation (perovskite-safe):
- Vapor-phase FeCl2/Fe(acac)2 coordination in dry inert atmosphere, or supercritical CO2 infusion with Fe precursor.
- Post-treatment: mild oxidation state set (chemical oxidant in vapor phase) avoiding ozone and avoiding protic solvents.
F3. Single-atom verification:
- EXAFS: absence of Fe–Fe scattering; dominant Fe–N coordination.
- STEM-EELS on witness films (on inert substrates).

G. Mandatory Gate 2 (Topology/ion-transport): model + matched experimental observables
G1. PNP model definition:
- Geometry: (i) flat interlayer; (ii) bicontinuous minimal-surface manifold approximated from tomography or level-set representation.
- Parameters: mobile ion density (10^17–10^19 cm−3), diffusion coefficients (10−12–10−9 cm^2 s−1), ε contrast, applied bias (0–1 V), temperature (25–65 °C).
- Output predictions: peak interfacial Δc/c0, spatial variance of ionic charge density, and τacc under bias.
- Pre-registered expected effect size: ≥30% reduction in peak Δc/c0 and ≥2× increase in τacc (slower pile-up) for bicontinuous vs flat at same thickness.
G2. Experimental readouts (must match trends):
- Bias-stress KPFM on perovskite/2PACz/interlayer stacks: measure surface potential evolution amplitude (ΔV) and time constant (τ) under ±0.5 V equivalent stress.
- Impedance spectroscopy under illumination: extract low-frequency capacitance growth attributable to ionic accumulation; require reduced LF capacitance rise.
- ToF-SIMS tracer drift (e.g., isotopic halide tracer or cation tracer in model perovskites): quantify accumulation at the interface after bias stress.
G3. Go/no-go criteria:
- Bicontinuous (C2 or C4) must show ≥25% reduction in ΔV amplitude in KPFM and a shift in τ consistent with model directionality; and ≥20% reduction in interfacial tracer accumulation vs flat (C1/C3).
- If not met: abandon curvature claim; proceed with glass-only passivation and Fe-only ROS sink with insulation (C1+C5), and refocus proposal outcomes accordingly.

H. Device integration and performance/stability validation (with mandatory recombination diagnostics)
H1. C60 deposition: thermal evaporation 10–20 nm at low rate; optimize partial infiltration without pore collapse.
H2. Recombination-risk reporting (mandatory):
- Ideality factor (n) vs light intensity; require no increase (Δn ≤ +0.1) vs C0.
- Subgap EQE / sensitive EQE: no new subgap features; integrated subgap photocurrent increase <10%.
- Absolute PLQY and implied Voc; must not worsen relative to best non-Fe control.
H3. ROS mechanism tests:
- Operando EPR spin trapping under controlled O2 (ppm–1%): C4 and C5 should reduce steady-state O2− relative to C2/C1; difference between C4 and C5 partitions ROS benefit vs electronic coupling.
- XPS after light soak: reduced Pb0 and I0 signatures in Fe-containing manifolds (if Gate 1 passed).
H4. Targets:
- Efficiency: Voc +25–40 mV and FF +2–4% absolute vs C0 at matched Jsc.
- Stability: ISOS-L-2 MPP at 65 °C, 20–30% RH, ≥1000 h with <10% PCE loss; oxygen-accelerated test (1% O2 in N2) showing slower Voc decay in Fe manifolds (C4/C5) vs non-Fe.

Feasibility: 1) De-risked translation of the literature assets into perovskite constraints:
- **Asset 1 (Schwarz P / utilization ratio):** We retain the *functional* insight—bicontinuous minimal-surface architectures increase the fraction of accessible, addressable sites—while acknowledging that perovskites cannot tolerate harsh processing. The revised plan eliminates plasma etching and uses solvent extraction/photocleavage, then verifies true bicontinuity and curvature statistics. The utilization-ratio concept is preserved but now coupled to explicit, measurable accessibility and electronic-coupling constraints via Gates 1 and 2.
- **Asset 2 (amorphous MOF-derived framework / stability):** We keep the “amorphous, conformal, site-stabilizing framework” concept but remove Zn2+/carboxylate risks by implementing a metal-free, covalently crosslinked aminated coordination-glass analogue. This directly addresses reviewer concern about ionic contamination and uncontrolled dipoles while preserving the high-density Lewis-base passivation logic.

2) Quantitative rigor added exactly where reviewers flagged risk (three mandatory gates):
- **Gate 1 (band/redox alignment):** The proposal now pre-registers measurement modalities (UPS/IPES, Kelvin probe under illumination, solid-state redox/spectroelectrochemistry, subgap EQE, PLQY at 1-sun carrier density) and explicit go/no-go thresholds to ensure the interlayer and Fe–N4 do not introduce recombination channels or deleterious band offsets.
- **Gate 2 (topology/ion-transport):** The curvature mechanism is no longer qualitative; it is tied to a coupled PNP model with realistic parameters and predicted effect sizes, and to specific experimental observables (KPFM ΔV/τ, LF impedance, ToF-SIMS accumulation) with defined pass/fail criteria.
- **Gate 3 (process compatibility):** Plasma is eliminated. Perovskite-inert extraction/photocleavage routes are validated directly on perovskite films with strict material-integrity criteria (XRD, UV–Vis, XPS/ToF-SIMS, PL).

3) Explicit recombination-risk separation and contingency paths:
- The added **C5 control** (Fe–N4 electronically insulated) is a direct, device-relevant test to decouple ROS scavenging from recombination/energetic coupling.
- If P-surface is not reproducible, the plan pivots to a curvature-statistics-qualified bicontinuous phase (e.g., gyroid) while still testing the *model-predicted ionic-accumulation suppression*. If that too fails, the curvature claim is dropped and the proposal still yields a valuable, lower-risk passivation/ROS strategy.

4) Utilization-ratio metric becomes experimentally anchored:
- Rather than relying on an unvalidated buried-site operando protocol, utilization is operationally defined as the product of (i) gas accessibility (validated by uptake/permeation and tomography-confirmed connected porosity) and (ii) electronic benignity/addressability (validated by Gate 1 photophysics + bias-dependent Fe spectroscopic signatures only after benignity is proven). Calibration is provided by comparing C4 vs C5 (same accessibility, different electronic coupling) and by porosity-controlled channel diameters.

Overall, the revised program remains conceptually aligned with the original concept chain (amorphous framework + minimal-surface bicontinuity + confined Fe–N4) but replaces the highest-risk chemistries and processes with perovskite-safe analogues, and elevates the mechanistic claims into testable, quantitative, gated milestones that can terminate or pivot the approach early without sunk-cost device integration.
final_critique: The proposal is unusually strong in execution planning: it defines a control matrix that cleanly separates chemistry/topology/redox effects, and it pre-registers go/no-go gates with quantitative thresholds tied to measurable observables (UPS/IPES, PLQY at 1-sun carrier density, subgap EQE/PDS, KPFM bias-stress dynamics, LF-impedance, ToF-SIMS drift). The main score deductions are for (i) incomplete physical justification that a 3–6 nm ‘coordination-glass’ can simultaneously (a) immobilize undercoordinated Pb–X species and (b) measurably suppress halide-vacancy migration—Pb–N binding is plausible, but vacancy pinning and field-screening contributions are not clearly separable from generic defect passivation; (ii) the PNP-curvature mechanism, while testable, may be second-order in realistic device stacks where ionic redistribution is dominated by heterogeneous injection barriers, local perovskite stoichiometry gradients, and contact chemistry rather than purely geometric field variance; (iii) Fe–N4 ‘energetic/kinetic gating’ is conceptually sound but under-specified at the quantitative level—what tunneling decay constant, spacer chemistry, and acceptable electronic coupling (or charge-transfer rate) boundaries ensure ROS scavenging without introducing interfacial SRH channels, especially under quasi-Fermi level splitting and with C60 present; and (iv) the translation from the target chain’s aIRMOF-3 logic to a fully metal-free covalent glass is chemically reasonable but weakens the direct evidence grounding to IRMOF-3 beyond analogy (i.e., it is no longer an isoreticular MOF-derived manifold, but a new polymeric coordination network).
hypothesis_summary: A perovskite-compatible, metal-free aminated coordination glass with bicontinuous minimal-surface morphology and wall-confined Fe–N4 single-atom redox centers passivates defects, suppresses ionic accumulation, and intercepts reactive oxygen species to boost perovskite solar cell efficiency and stability.

original_chain: Zn-Car_MOF -> Electrocatalytic activity -> Overpotential -> Turnover frequency (TOF) -> Metal oxide -> Continuous hydrothermal synthesis -> Supercritical hydrothermal synthesis (scHS) -> Fe3O4
proposal_content:
Hypothesis: Interfacial recombination and bias-induced degradation in inverted (p–i–n) perovskite solar cells can be suppressed by engineering the buried electron contact into a kinetically favorable, electronically benign charge-discharge interface in which Fe3O4 acts as a reversible redox buffer (Fe2+/Fe3+) that lowers the effective interfacial electron-extraction barrier without introducing mid-gap recombination pathways, while a site-confined Zn-Car_MOF simultaneously passivates chemical defects and immobilizes mobile halides. Specifically, ultrasmall Fe3O4 nanoparticles (3–6 nm) seeded at the C60/metal-oxide interface provide a high-density polaron-hopping network whose Fermi level under operating conditions is pinned close to the C60 LUMO, enabling transient electron storage and rapid transfer into the metal-oxide conduction band rather than back-injection into the perovskite. The Zn-Car_MOF forms only at Fe3O4 surfaces during a tightly controlled, low-water-activity anneal, creating nanoscale coordination domains that (i) bind undercoordinated Pb2+ and halide-vacancy complexes at the buried interface, increasing quasi-Fermi level splitting and Voc, and (ii) locally suppress halide mobility and interfacial redox reactions. The combined interphase reduces chemical capacitance and charge-transfer resistance at the buried contact, increases recombination resistance, and improves MPP stability. This mechanism is falsifiable via predicted shifts in band alignment, Fe oxidation-state cycling under bias, and quantitative changes in operando EIS-derived kinetic parameters.
Plan: Step 1: Energetics closure and baseline definition.
1.1 Construct baseline inverted devices: glass/ITO/NiOx (or PTAA)/FA-Cs mixed-halide perovskite/C60/ALD-SnO2/Ag.
1.2 Determine absolute energy levels for each contact: UPS and Kelvin probe for work function and valence-band edges of C60, SnO2, Fe3O4 nanoparticle films, and Zn-Car_MOF; UV–Vis/Tauc for Fe3O4 bandgap. Target alignment: Fe3O4 Fermi level within ±0.2 eV of C60 LUMO under illumination.
1.3 Pre-register expected signatures: (i) reduction in low-frequency chemical capacitance (Cμ) and charge-transfer resistance (Rct) at the electron contact; (ii) increase in recombination resistance (Rrec); (iii) neutral-to-positive Voc shift (≥ +20 mV) if recombination is suppressed without added barriers.

Step 2: Nanoparticle synthesis and ink formulation (operationalizing CHS vs scHS).
2.1 Synthesize Fe3O4 via continuous hydrothermal synthesis under supercritical conditions (scHS): 400–420 °C, 25–30 MPa, residence time <1 s, using Fe(II/III) chloride precursors. Rationale: scHS ensures rapid nucleation, narrow PSD (σ <15%), and high crystallinity, minimizing surface trap states compared to subcritical CHS.
2.2 Quench and cap particles with volatile formate ligands (≤0.5 monolayer coverage) removable at ≤120 °C.
2.3 Formulate a reactive contact ink containing Fe3O4 (areal density <10^11 cm^-2), Zn(OAc)2, carnosine, and a weak competing ligand (acetate) in anhydrous alcohol with controlled water activity (<500 ppm).

Step 3: Seed-confined in situ Zn-Car_MOF formation.
3.1 Deposit the ink by blade or slot-die coating onto C60 or SnO2 at sub-monolayer coverage.
3.2 Trigger MOF formation during a post-deposition anneal: 90–110 °C, 5–10 min, controlled relative humidity 5–10%. This window is pre-validated to avoid perovskite or C60 degradation while allowing Zn–carnosine coordination only at Fe3O4 surfaces.
3.3 Demonstrate reproducibility across ≥5 batches using GIWAXS (absence of bulk MOF peaks) and cross-sectional STEM-EDS/EELS (Zn/N confined to Fe-rich sites).

Step 4: Direct validation of the Fe3O4 self-discharge mechanism.
4.1 Operando near-ambient-pressure XPS or operando Fe K-edge XAS on model stacks (ITO/C60/Fe3O4/Zn-Car/SnO2) under illumination and bias to track reversible Fe2+/Fe3+ ratios.
4.2 Mössbauer spectroscopy on biased model devices to quantify redox cycling amplitude and rule out irreversible Fe reduction.

Step 5: Parameter-identifiable kinetic modeling.
5.1 Fit operando EIS with a constrained equivalent circuit (transport resistance, interfacial Rct, Cμ, Rrec) informed by drift–diffusion simulations.
5.2 Perform sensitivity and uncertainty analysis to extract confidence intervals for interfacial recombination velocity and electron-transfer rate constants.
5.3 Cross-validate extracted rates with transient photocurrent/photovoltage (TPC/TPV) on identical stacks.

Step 6: Device performance and stability.
6.1 Quantify Voc, FF, and hysteresis; correlate changes with extracted kinetic parameters.
6.2 Bias-stress and MPP tracking at 60–85 °C; ToF-SIMS to monitor halide accumulation.
6.3 Demonstrate slot-die-coated mini-modules and assess device-to-device variance enabled by scHS-controlled Fe3O4 PSD.
Feasibility: The proposal directly addresses reviewer concerns by explicitly closing the electron-balance loop and defining the terminal sink for accumulated electrons as the metal-oxide conduction band, mediated by reversible Fe2+/Fe3+ redox capacitance rather than uncontrolled trap-assisted recombination. Energy-level alignment will be experimentally verified (UPS/Kelvin probe), and falsifiable predictions for Voc, Rct, and Cμ are pre-registered. Direct operando probes (NAP-XPS/XAS/Mössbauer) validate Fe oxidation-state cycling, de-risking the catalytic-like self-discharge claim. The Zn-Car_MOF formation is constrained to a narrow, industry-compatible humidity/temperature window, with batch-to-batch reproducibility verified structurally and chemically. The replacement of the TOF-like metric with a parameter-identifiable kinetic model, supported by uncertainty analysis and independent transient validation, ensures quantitative rigor. Finally, supercritical CHS is operationalized with explicit conditions, justifying its inclusion as an enabling method for producing electronically clean, narrow-PSD Fe3O4 seeds critical to the mechanism.
final_critique: The engineering plan is unusually concrete and testable for a buried-contact interphase: device stack is specified; energy-level verification and pre-registered signatures are articulated; scHS synthesis conditions and ligand strategy are defined; and operando NAP-XPS/XAS/Mössbauer are appropriate to falsify Fe2+/Fe3+ cycling. The main scientific vulnerability is mechanistic overreach around the ‘kinetically favorable, electronically benign’ redox-buffer claim: Fe3O4 in contact with C60/SnO2 can introduce mid-gap states, magnetic/defect-mediated hopping, and Fermi-level pinning that may *increase* interfacial recombination unless the surface chemistry and coverage are controlled with stronger evidence than “high crystallinity/narrow PSD.” The proposal also conflates redox-capacitive buffering with electrocatalysis: no explicit interfacial reaction is defined (e.g., O2/H2O reduction, iodide/iodine shuttling, SnO2 surface redox), so ‘overpotential’ and ‘TOF’ remain metaphorical rather than measurable. In addition, the constraint “Zn–carnosine coordination only at Fe3O4 surfaces” is asserted but not chemically guaranteed; Zn-carboxylate/imidazole-like coordination can also occur on SnO2 hydroxyls and at C60 defect/oxygenated sites, risking uncontrolled interlayers and an increased extraction barrier. Finally, the EIS parameter identifiability claim is directionally good, but the proposed equivalent circuit (Rct, Cμ, Rrec) is underdetermined without explicit frequency-range design, illumination/bias matrix, and model-selection criteria; drift–diffusion ‘informing’ does not by itself prevent non-unique fits. Overall: strong instrumentation and falsifiability, but incomplete linkage to the required TOF/overpotential concept chain and insufficient risk-mitigation for Fe3O4-induced recombination and non-confined MOF growth.
hypothesis_summary: A reversible redox buffer and site-confined metal-organic framework at the buried electron contact suppress recombination and halide migration, enabling stable, efficient inverted perovskite solar cells.

original_chain: Nanocomposites -> Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) -> NH3BH3 -> Turnover frequency (TOF) -> Electrochemical active surface area (ECSA)
proposal_content:
Hypothesis: A grain-boundary-confined, electronically insulating UiO-66–oxide nanocomposite formed in situ by anti-solvent-triggered MOF nano-precipitation (AT‑MNP) will (a) increase the density of *chemically accessible* defect-binding sites (Pb2+ undercoordination, halide vacancies) and (b) reduce *field-driven halide chemical potential gradients* at grain boundaries by immobilizing mobile ions in fixed, high-affinity coordination environments—without creating a continuous electronic or ionic shunt—thereby lowering non-radiative recombination (higher Voc, higher quasi-Fermi level splitting) and suppressing ion-migration-driven degradation.

Mechanistic rationale refined to address reviewer concerns about measurement and causality:
1) **Defect-binding accessibility (not just presence)**: UiO-66 Zr6O4(OH)4 nodes and functionalized linkers (–NH2 as Lewis base/H-bond donor; –SO3H as strong Brønsted acid with fixed anion after deprotonation/ion pairing) create localized binding motifs that can form (i) Zr–O···Pb interactions / Pb–O coordination (hard-hard), (ii) H-bonding/ion pairing to halide vacancies and undercoordinated iodide environments, and (iii) interfacial dipole screening that reduces band-tail states. Accessibility is defined operationally by *selective probe uptake* (vapor-phase titration) and *selective probe binding signatures* (XPS/ToF-SIMS), not by aqueous catalysis alone.
2) **No-shunt premise made falsifiable**: The nanocomposite is engineered to be (i) electronically insulating (UiO-66/Al2O3 or UiO-66/SiO2), (ii) spatially discontinuous (grain-boundary decoration, not a continuous interlayer), and (iii) non-percolating for ion transport under operating fields. Whether it blocks or facilitates halide motion is treated as an experimental outcome quantified by *tracer diffusion* and *DC ionic transference under bias*, with explicit go/no-go thresholds.
3) **Aqueous NH3BH3 assay demoted from “primary quantifier” to “orthogonal accessibility stress-test”**: NH3BH3 hydrolysis TOF is retained only as a secondary, tightly controlled readout of surface chemical accessibility *after* backgrounds from perovskite decomposition and acid/base effects are bracketed using inert-film controls, decomposed-perovskite controls, and isotope labeling (D2O and/or deuterated borane). The proposal’s primary accessibility metric becomes perovskite-relevant Lewis acid/base probe titration and binding-site spectroscopy, which directly interrogate the target coordination chemistry at/near grain boundaries.
Plan: Step 1 — Platforms, materials, and AT‑MNP placement (unchanged core, tightened parameters)
1.1 Device platforms (generality retained):
(A) n–i–p: glass/ITO/SnO2/(FA,Cs)Pb(I,Br)3/HTL (PTAA or equivalent)/Au.
(B) p–i–n: glass/ITO/NiOx/(FA,Cs)Pb(I,Br)3/C60/BCP/Ag.
Keep perovskite ink stoichiometry and anti-solvent protocol identical across MOF variants; only the anti-solvent composition changes.

1.2 MOF chemistry constrained to redox-inert Zr‑UiO family (no transition-metal nodes). Three chemistries:
(i) UiO‑66 (BDC), (ii) UiO‑66‑NH2, (iii) UiO‑66‑SO3H or mixed-linker UiO‑66‑(NH2)x(SO3H)1−x (x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) to decouple acidity from site density.
Target MOF nanoparticle primary size: 3–10 nm (TEM verified), because smaller particles maximize interfacial contact at GBs while minimizing optical scattering.

1.3 AT‑MNP formulation and timing (methodological specificity):
- Anti-solvent: anisole:chlorobenzene (1:1 v/v) as a baseline; adjust polarity with ≤10 vol% ethyl acetate only if needed to solubilize linker.
- MOF precursors in anti-solvent: preformed Zr6-oxo cluster source (e.g., ZrOCl2-derived Zr6O4(OH)4 acetate/benzoate cluster) + linker (BDC/NH2‑BDC/SO3H‑BDC). Total precursor concentration: 0.05–0.5 mM (screened).
- Water activity control: introduce 50–300 ppm water (Karl Fischer verified) to enable Zr–oxo condensation but prevent bulk perovskite hydration. Water delivered via pre-equilibrated anti-solvent; no direct water addition to perovskite ink.
- Dispense timing: last 5–8 s of spin (high rpm stage) so perovskite reaches supersaturation first; MOF nucleation occurs in residual solvent pockets and arrests at GBs. 
- MOF mass fraction target in film: 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 wt% (relative to perovskite solids), with a hard stop at the onset of PL quenching or FF loss.

1.4 Nanocomposite spacer engineering (to prevent percolating pathways):
- Co-precipitate 2–5 nm Al2O3 or SiO2 colloids (0.5–2× mass of MOF precursor) in anti-solvent to physically interrupt MOF–MOF necking.
- Objective microstructure: “decorated GB islands” rather than continuous coatings. Quantify with (i) cross-sectional STEM-EDS Zr mapping and (ii) statistical percolation proxy: fraction of GB length containing Zr signal (f_GB,Zr) and mean Zr-cluster spacing along GB.

Step 2 — Replace/augment ECSA with perovskite-relevant binding-site titration and calibrated spectroscopy (Mandatory Directive ii)
2.1 Primary accessibility metric: vapor-phase probe uptake titration (QCM + ellipsometry)
- Fabricate thin-film coupons on QCM crystals and on Si (for ellipsometry): (a) perovskite-only, (b) perovskite+AT‑MNP MOF/oxide, (c) oxide-only AT step, (d) MOF/oxide-only film (no perovskite).
- Probes (orthogonal Lewis base/acid):
  • Lewis base probe for undercoordinated Pb2+: pyridine (Py) and 4‑tert‑butylpyridine (tBP) vapor; optionally trimethylphosphine oxide (TMPO) for stronger Pb2+ coordination.
  • Lewis acid probe for halide-rich/anion-binding motifs: CO2 (weak) and SO2 (stronger) uptake; alternatively, use acetonitrile vapor as a polarity probe (control).
- Protocol: stepwise dosing (0.1–10 mbar equivalent) at 25 °C, measure mass uptake (QCM) and thickness/refractive-index change (ellipsometry). Fit isotherms (Langmuir/dual-site) to extract accessible site density N_access (sites·cm−2) and adsorption enthalpy proxy (from temperature steps 25/35/45 °C where feasible).
- Specificity controls: compare probe uptake on MOF/oxide-only vs perovskite-only vs composite; the *incremental uptake attributable to MOF-at-GB* is ΔN_access,GB.

2.2 Calibrated binding confirmation: XPS/ToF-SIMS with probe molecules
- After vapor dosing (short, controlled), perform XPS to detect bound-probe chemical shifts:
  • Pb 4f shift/lineshape changes consistent with Pb–N or Pb–O coordination.
  • N 1s (pyridine) or P 2p (TMPO) signals to quantify bound probe coverage.
- ToF-SIMS depth profiling (gentle cluster sputter) to localize probe signals at/near GB-enriched regions; correlate with Zr signal to confirm co-localization.
- Output: a quantitative “Probe-Binding Accessibility Index” (PBAI) = (bound-probe signal normalized to Zr-at% at GB) to decouple loading from accessibility.

2.3 Optional electrochemical capacitance retained only as supportive evidence (downgraded)
- If used, run EIS/Cdl only on MOF/oxide-only and oxide-only films in anhydrous ACN to avoid perovskite mixed-conductor ambiguity; do not claim absolute ECSA for perovskite. Use as internal consistency check with QCM-derived N_access.

Step 3 — NH3BH3 hydrolysis converted into a defensible orthogonal assay with hard controls + isotopes (Mandatory Directive i)
3.1 Purpose redefined: NH3BH3 assay is an *accessibility stress-test* for whether surface-exposed MOF functionalities remain chemically reachable under brief wetting, not a primary defect-site counter.

3.2 Control matrix (must be executed before interpreting composite signals)
Run identical microfluidic droplet exposures on:
(A) MOF/oxide-only films on inert substrates (glass/SiO2) — isolates MOF chemistry.
(B) oxide-only films — background.
(C) pristine perovskite films — establishes perovskite-driven background.
(D) intentionally decomposed perovskite (e.g., controlled humid exposure until PbI2 signature appears in XRD) — brackets worst-case decomposition-catalyzed background.
(E) perovskite chemically passivated without MOF (e.g., 2PACz/PEAI surface treatment) — shows non-MOF passivation background.

3.3 Isotope labeling to identify H2 source and exclude perovskite side reactions
- Use D2O as solvent: true hydrolysis should yield HD/D2 patterns predictable from mechanism; quantify H2/HD/D2 with MS.
- Where feasible, use deuterated borane (NH3BD3) to further pinpoint hydrogen origin.
- Acceptance rule: composite-specific signal is only attributed to MOF accessibility if isotope distribution matches borane hydrolysis expectations AND perovskite-only and decomposed-perovskite controls show negligible/characteristically different isotope signatures.

3.4 Normalize NH3BH3 signal to independently measured accessibility (from QCM/XPS)
- Report “Wet-Access Retention Factor” (WARF) = (H2 rate per N_access from vapor titration)composite / (H2 rate per N_access)MOF/oxide-only.
- Interpretation: WARF ~ 1 indicates MOF sites remain accessible when embedded; WARF ≪ 1 indicates embedding blocks access (good for ‘no shunt’, but may reduce defect binding); WARF ≫ 1 indicates uncontrolled chemistry (likely perovskite side reactions) and triggers a stop/re-design.

Step 4 — Direct tests of ‘ionic sink without shunt’ using tracer diffusion + DC transference (Mandatory Directive iii)
4.1 Halide tracer diffusion (primary discriminant between blocking vs facilitated transport)
Two options depending on facility access:
(A) Radiotracer: 82Br or 124I exchange on top surface under controlled bias/temperature, then depth profiling (autoradiography or sectioning).
(B) Stable-isotope exchange: expose films to enriched halide source (e.g., KI enriched in 127I not helpful; better: use 81Br/79Br ratio shifts if available) and quantify depth profiles via ToF-SIMS using isotope ratios; alternatively, do halide exchange using different halide (Br↔I) and track profiles by SIMS/XPS.
- Extract effective diffusion coefficient D_halide under (i) dark, (ii) illumination, and (iii) applied bias.
- Criterion: MOF/oxide composites must reduce D_halide by ≥3× relative to perovskite control at operating-relevant fields/temperatures; any increase in D_halide is a mechanistic falsification (see Step 6).

4.2 DC ionic transference under bias
- Use symmetric blocking-electrode stacks (e.g., Au/perovskite/Au or carbon/perovskite/carbon) with and without AT‑MNP.
- Apply small DC bias (0.1–0.5 V) at 25–60 °C; measure steady-state current vs time to separate electronic leakage from ionic drift (Hebb–Wagner polarization framework).
- Output: ionic conductivity σ_ion and ionic transference number t_ion under conditions matching PSC operation.
- Go/no-go: AT‑MNP must not increase σ_ion by >20% at 0.5 V·µm−1 equivalent field; preferred outcome is σ_ion decrease ≥2×.

Step 5 — Film and device validation (kept, but explicitly tied to new metrics)
5.1 Localization and structure
- Cross-sectional STEM-EDS: quantify f_GB,Zr and Zr-at% at GB vs grain interior.
- GIWAXS/XRD: ensure no secondary phases beyond controlled PbI2 tolerance window (<2% relative peak area unless intentionally studied).
- Optical loss budget: haze/scattering + absorption; enforce <1% absolute loss in integrated visible transmittance for target wt%.

5.2 Defect/recombination linkage to accessibility
- Absolute PLQY → quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) and non-radiative loss.
- TRPL + intensity-dependent PL to separate bulk vs interfacial recombination.
- Trap spectroscopy: thermal admittance (tDOS) + SCLC in e-only/h-only stacks.
- Required correlation: ΔN_access,GB (from QCM/XPS) must correlate with reduced trap density and improved QFLS; otherwise accessibility is not functionally passivating.

5.3 Device performance + stability
- JV hysteresis index, stabilized MPP, Voc deficit (vs bandgap).
- ISOS-L-2 and ISOS-O-2; extract T80 and relate to D_halide and σ_ion.

Step 6 — Pre-registered falsifiable criteria and quantitative thresholds (Mandatory Directive iv)
6.1 Go/no-go thresholds
- Localization threshold: f_GB,Zr ≥ 0.6 (≥60% of GB length shows Zr enrichment) OR Zr-at% at GB ≥ 0.5 at% (STEM-EDS quantified). If not reached, AT‑MNP conditions are considered unsuccessful regardless of device metrics.
- Passivation threshold: QFLS increase ≥ 20 meV AND Voc increase ≥ 20 mV at constant Jsc (within ±1%) for at least one MOF chemistry at ≤0.1 wt% loading.
- No-shunt threshold (ionic): σ_ion increase must be ≤20% (hard limit) and D_halide must decrease by ≥3× under bias/illumination. Exceeding σ_ion limit or increasing D_halide falsifies the ‘ionic sink without shunt’ premise for that chemistry/loading.

6.2 Mechanism falsification statements (pre-registered)
- If ΔN_access,GB increases (QCM/XPS) but trap density and QFLS do not improve, then the added sites are not binding the relevant defects (mechanism rejected; redesign linker functionality).
- If WARF indicates strong wet accessibility yet isotope-labeled NH3BH3 results match decomposed-perovskite controls, then NH3BH3 signal is dominated by perovskite side reactions (assay invalid for the composite; it will be removed from decision-making).
- If D_halide increases while Voc improves, then stability mechanism is not ion immobilization; alternative explanation (e.g., energetic alignment/dipoles) will be tested, and the ‘ionic sink’ claim will be removed.

Step 7 — Experimental design and statistics
- Response surface across: linker chemistry (BDC/NH2/SO3H/mixed), wt% (0.01–0.2), oxide spacer ratio (0–2×).
- Primary outputs: ΔN_access,GB (QCM/XPS), f_GB,Zr, D_halide, σ_ion/t_ion, QFLS, trap density, Voc/FF/hysteresis, T80.
- Decision hierarchy: (1) localization + no-shunt thresholds, then (2) passivation metrics, then (3) stability metrics. NH3BH3/WARF is supportive only.
Feasibility: 1) Why the refined measurement logic is now defensible
- The reviewer’s central concern was that aqueous NH3BH3 TOF is confounded by perovskite wetting/decomposition and pH effects. This revision makes **vapor-phase probe titration (QCM/ellipsometry + XPS/ToF-SIMS)** the primary accessibility metric, directly interrogating Lewis acid/base interactions relevant to Pb2+ undercoordination and halide-vacancy environments without exposing perovskite to liquid water.
- NH3BH3 is retained only as an **orthogonal wet-accessibility stress-test** and is made interpretable by (i) inert-film and decomposed-perovskite bracketing controls, (ii) isotope labeling (D2O and/or NH3BD3) to confirm hydrogen source, and (iii) normalization to independently measured N_access (WARF), so changes in acidity or uncontrolled perovskite chemistry are detectable rather than silently biasing conclusions.

2) Why ‘ionic sink without shunt’ is testable rather than assumed
- Instead of inferring ion blocking from low-frequency EIS arcs, the plan now includes **direct halide tracer diffusion (radiotracer or isotope exchange + depth profiling)** and **DC ionic transference/polarization** under operating-relevant fields and temperatures. These deliver an unambiguous sign (reduced vs increased D_halide and σ_ion) and enable hard thresholds.
- The nanocomposite architecture (UiO‑66 + Al2O3/SiO2 spacers) is explicitly designed to reduce percolation and pore connectivity; success is quantified via f_GB,Zr and spacing statistics, linking microstructure to ionic outcomes.

3) Why the mechanistic chain remains coherent with the original concept and literature assets
- Asset 1 supports the central materials principle: reticular frameworks can host/stabilize nanoscale functional components with preserved structure and accessible sites. Here, AT‑MNP similarly creates a stabilized, spatially confined MOF nanophase at grain boundaries, engineered for accessibility and mechanical/chemical robustness.
- Asset 2 motivates the concept that MOF-derived interfaces can be quantified by turnover-type assays and that interfacial synergy governs activity; we transfer only the *logic of orthogonal functional readouts*, not the claim that NH3BH3 directly counts perovskite defect sites. The revised plan uses NH3BH3 only with isotope/controls and ties it to independently quantified accessibility.
- The revised causality framework explicitly requires: (i) increased perovskite-relevant probe accessibility (ΔN_access,GB), (ii) improved recombination metrics (QFLS/Voc, reduced trap density), and (iii) reduced halide mobility (D_halide/σ_ion) to validate the full mechanism. Any decoupling falsifies or narrows the claim.

4) Practical feasibility
- AT‑MNP is compatible with standard spin-coating (only modifies anti-solvent); UiO‑66 chemistry is robust and widely reproducible.
- QCM/ellipsometry vapor dosing and XPS/ToF-SIMS are standard in thin-film surface science; they avoid the perovskite-in-electrolyte ambiguities highlighted by reviewers.
- If radiotracer access is limited, the plan includes a stable-isotope/halide-exchange ToF-SIMS pathway as a feasible alternative for diffusion profiling.
final_critique:
Methodological resolution is strong: AT‑MNP parameters (timing, ppm water, precursor concentration, particle-size target) and microstructural anti-percolation design are sufficiently engineered, and the shift to vapor-phase probe titration with post-dosing spectroscopy is a defensible correction to aqueous-confounding. The proposal is also unusually good in pre-registered falsification (D_halide, σ_ion thresholds) and in separating 'localization', 'passivation', and 'no-shunt' claims.

Key deductions: (i) the core mechanistic leap—"more chemically accessible sites" → "relevant defect passivation"—remains under-identified at the chemical-speciation level. Pyridine/tBP/TMPO uptake will conflate adsorption to MOF nodes/linkers with adsorption to perovskite Pb2+ sites unless a stronger deconvolution strategy is enforced (e.g., competitive binding, desorption energetics, or selective site poisoning). (ii) The ionic-sink claim is testable, but the physical picture is ambiguous: UiO-66 porosity and sulfonate functionalization can plausibly *increase* local halide solvation/coordination and create interfacial space-charge that may either immobilize or accelerate migration depending on loading and connectivity; the plan lacks an explicit electrostatic/chemical potential model that predicts the sign of the effect versus linker chemistry and oxide fraction. (iii) The concept chain NH3BH3→TOF→ECSA is now logically orthogonal to the primary perovskite mechanism; retaining it as “supportive” weakens evidence grounding relative to the requested chain because ECSA is explicitly disclaimed for perovskite and TOF is no longer a mechanistic quantifier.

Overall: excellent experimental rigor and falsifiability, but the causal attribution between probe uptake, true defect neutralization, and ionic chemical-potential-gradient suppression needs a tighter, chemistry-resolved mechanistic backbone and clearer separation of MOF-intrinsic adsorption from perovskite-defect binding.
hypothesis_summary: A grain-boundary-confined, insulating MOF–oxide nanocomposite increases chemically accessible defect-binding sites and immobilizes mobile ions at grain boundaries, reducing non-radiative recombination and suppressing ion-migration-driven degradation without creating electronic or ionic shunts.

original_chain: Third-order NLO polarizability -> Modulation depth -> Saturable absorber (SA) -> Charge transfer -> Hysteresis -> Electron transport layer (ETL)
proposal_content:
Hypothesis: Embedding an ultralow-volume-fraction (≤0.5 vol%) third-order NLO–active molecular network into a compact TiO2 ETL can *measurably and reversibly* modulate the ETL’s low-frequency dielectric response (εeff, 10–10^3 Hz) and effective electron conductivity (σe) under solar illumination, thereby reducing interfacial charge accumulation and J–V hysteresis. The refined mechanism explicitly bridges ultrafast χ(3)/saturable absorption (SA) physics with slow electrodynamics as follows: under steady-state illumination (~1 sun), partial saturation of the NLO chromophores induces a population-averaged, intensity-dependent polarization ⟨P⟩ that renormalizes the Maxwell–Wagner interfacial polarization of the nanocomposite ETL. This produces a *DC-relevant increase in εeff* via field-averaged χ(3) contributions (Δε ≈ 3χ(3)⟨E^2⟩) and a concomitant reduction in space-charge field gradients at the perovskite/ETL junction. The resulting field flattening lowers the interfacial charge density (Δσint) and suppresses the driving force for ionic redistribution without relying on permanent chemical passivation. The hypothesis is falsifiable: if illumination does not induce a reversible Δεeff ≥ 10–20% at 10–10^2 Hz and a correlated reduction in low-frequency EIS capacitance/arc area and hysteresis index, the dynamic χ(3)-based mechanism is invalidated.
Plan: Step 1: Quantitative baseline definition.
1.1 Fabricate reference n–i–p PSCs (glass/FTO/compact TiO2 via SPD, 70 ± 5 nm/triple-cation perovskite/HTL/Au).
1.2 Establish baseline metrics: hysteresis index (HI), low-frequency EIS capacitance (Cion at 0.1–100 Hz), interfacial charge density (from C–V), electron mobility (μe via SCLC/THz), and Jsc.

Step 2: NLO-ETL composite design with controlled electrodynamics.
2.1 Select NLO additives with χ(3) ≥ 10^−8 esu and weak ground-state absorption at 450–800 nm (α < 200 cm^−1 at ≤0.5 vol%), including (i) conjugated zwitterionic chromophores and (ii) MOF-derived π-fragments inspired by HHTP systems.
2.2 Incorporate additives into the TiO2 SPD precursor using bidentate chelating ligands (e.g., carboxylate/phosphonate) to anchor chromophores at grain boundaries while preserving TiO2 percolation.
2.3 SPD deposition parameters: substrate temperature 450 °C, aerosol flow 4–6 L min^−1; post-anneal 450 °C/30 min to remove organics except anchored NLO moieties.
2.4 Verify dispersion and survivability via cross-sectional TEM-EDS, ToF-SIMS depth profiling, Raman/FTIR mapping.

Step 3: Electrodynamic model validation.
3.1 Measure χ(3) and SA parameters of the composite ETL films by Z-scan and pump–probe; extract saturation intensity Is and χ(3).
3.2 Predict Δεeff using Δε(ω→0) ≈ 3χ(3)⟨Eopt^2⟩f, where f is the volume fraction and ⟨Eopt^2⟩ is derived from optical field intensity under 1 sun. Set a target Δεeff ≥ 10% at 10–100 Hz.
3.3 Experimentally measure illumination-dependent εeff and σe using light-biased EIS and C–V under dark vs 1 sun; confirm reversibility with light on/off cycling.

Step 4: Charge-transfer and hysteresis correlation.
4.1 Quantify interfacial charge accumulation via low-frequency EIS arc area and capacitance; target ≥30% reduction relative to pristine TiO2.
4.2 Correlate Δεeff with reduced HI, scan-rate dependence, and bias-stress recovery.
4.3 Use IMPS/IMVS and light-biased EIS to demonstrate that transport/capacitance changes track illumination intensity rather than permanent chemical modification.

Step 5: Controls and decoupling experiments.
5.1 Non-NLO analog control: chemically similar additives with comparable dipole moments but χ(3) ≪ 10^−10 esu.
5.2 Stoichiometry control: match TiO2 oxygen vacancy density across samples (XPS, EPR) and band alignment (UPS/KPFM).
5.3 Mobility control: Hall/4-probe and SCLC to ensure μe reduction ≤20%.

Step 6: Go/no-go criteria.
- Δεeff(10–100 Hz, 1 sun) ≥ 10% (go).
- Reduction in low-frequency EIS capacitance ≥30% (go).
- ΔJsc ≤ −2% and μe ≥ 80% of reference (go).
Failure to meet these thresholds terminates the dynamic χ(3) hypothesis.
Feasibility: The proposal now explicitly reconciles ultrafast NLO physics with slow hysteresis phenomena by invoking field-averaged χ(3)-induced dielectric renormalization rather than direct ultrafast carrier dynamics. This approach is grounded in Maxwell–Wagner polarization theory for nanocomposites and supported by empirical χ(3) magnitudes demonstrated in ultrathin MOF/graphene systems (Asset 1). The quantitative model yields clear, testable predictions for Δεeff and σe under 1-sun illumination, directly addressing the reviewer’s concern regarding mechanistic overreach. By predefining strict go/no-go thresholds (Δεeff, μe, ΔJsc, EIS features) and employing chemically matched non-NLO controls alongside stoichiometry and band-alignment matching (Assets 2 and 3 context), the plan rigorously decouples dynamic optical nonlinearity from static passivation or doping effects. Finally, SPD compatibility and electron percolation are explicitly validated with in-film mapping and mobility measurements, ensuring scalability and preserving the comparative advantage of a bulk-modulated, illumination-adaptive ETL over conventional interfacial strategies.
final_critique: This is a technically ambitious and unusually rigorous proposal that stands out for its falsifiability and quantitative discipline. The engineering plan is detailed, SPD-compatible, and supported by appropriate in-film diagnostics. The primary weakness lies in the logical leap between ultrafast χ(3)/SA saturation physics and a sustained, DC-relevant increase in ε_eff at 10–100 Hz under 1-sun illumination. While the Maxwell–Wagner framework is invoked correctly, the proposal does not yet convincingly demonstrate that the field-averaged ⟨E_opt^2⟩ under solar flux is sufficient to drive a ≥10–20% dielectric renormalization at sub-kHz frequencies, especially given the extremely low volume fraction (≤0.5%) and post-anneal survival constraints. The χ(3)-to-ε translation, though mathematically stated, risks overestimating the effective contribution without a more explicit treatment of relaxation times, chromophore orientation averaging, and thermal vs optical saturation under steady-state conditions. Evidence grounding is strong and remains within the optoelectronic/NLO domain, but empirical precedent for such large low-frequency dielectric shifts in oxide ETLs under 1 sun remains sparse. The rationale is creative and addresses hysteresis without chemical passivation, yet its success hinges on a narrow and demanding physical window.
hypothesis_summary: Embedding a tiny amount of nonlinear optical molecules into a solar cell’s electron transport layer can use light to reversibly tune its low-frequency electrical properties, reducing charge buildup and performance lag.

original_chain: Atomically precise nanoclusters (APNCs) -> Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) -> Copper(I) oxide (Cu2O) -> Zinc oxide (ZnO) -> Water purification membranes -> Copper(I) oxide (Cu2O)
proposal_content:
Hypothesis: Embedding atomically precise Cu nanoclusters (Cu-APNCs; e.g., Cu25(SR)18-class as a model) into a chemically robust, ultrathin MOF-on-ZnO interlayer—specifically a Zr(IV)-carboxylate MOF (UiO-66-X, X = NH2 or COOH) conformally grown/anchored on ZnO—followed by quantitatively controlled, low-temperature oxidation in a narrowly defined oxygen chemical-potential window will yield a pore-confined, electronically percolative Cu2O nanodomain network (sub-nm to ~2 nm effective domain size) at the ZnO/perovskite interface. This architecture will (i) chemically decouple perovskite from ZnO basic/hydroxyl sites and suppress ZnO-driven interfacial decomposition by blocking OH−/H2O access and passivating ZnO surface states; and (ii) introduce a stable interfacial dipole and graded energetic selectivity (Cu2O p-type domains within an insulating-but-ultrathin MOF scaffold) that reduces non-radiative interfacial recombination without creating a transport-blocking layer. Mechanistic constraints are explicitly built in: (a) UiO-66’s Zr–O clusters and strong Zr–carboxylate bonds provide oxidative/solvent stability during O2/H2O exposure and perovskite antisolvent processing; (b) UiO-66 pore apertures (~6 Å windows; ~8–11 Å cages depending on defect density) impose diffusion-limited O2/H2O transport and spatial confinement, forcing oxidation to proceed via self-limited nucleation of Cu2O nanodomains rather than uncontrolled CuO/Cu(OH)2 growth; (c) electronic continuity is not assumed—rather, a targeted “near-percolation” Cu2O fraction is tuned so that the Cu2O nanodomains generate a reproducible dipole/work-function shift (measured operando by AR-UPS/KPFM) while the ultrathin MOF (≤15–20 nm) and discrete Cu2O avoid raising contact resistance beyond an experimentally defined threshold (validated by c-AFM and electron-only contact-resistance extraction). The resulting ZnO/UiO-66-X(Cu2O)/perovskite interface is hypothesized to decrease ΔVoc,nonrad (Suns-Voc) by suppressing interfacial SRH pathways, reduce hysteresis by limiting ionic accumulation at reactive ZnO sites, and improve operational stability by limiting OH−-triggered reactions and metal/halide interdiffusion. To satisfy the concept-chain constraint with water purification membranes, the same APNC@MOF→Cu2O conversion protocol will be transferred to a porous polymer support (PVDF) to form Cu2O@UiO-66 antibacterial/photocatalytic membranes, enabling cross-domain validation of oxidation control, robustness, and functional stability under aqueous oxidative conditions.
Plan: A. Materials selection and architectural definition (hard-bounded choices)
A1. ETL: Low-temperature ZnO (nanoparticle or sol–gel) on ITO, anneal ≤150 °C. Two ZnO chemistries: (i) baseline; (ii) hydroxyl-rich ZnO (intentional high –OH via reduced anneal + humid storage) as a stress-case for interfacial reactivity assays.
A2. MOF system (predefined): UiO-66-NH2 and UiO-66-COOH (Zr6O4(OH)4 nodes; terephthalate linkers with –NH2 or –COOH). Rationale: established stability toward oxidants, moisture, and many polar antisolvents; functional groups offer Lewis-base/H-bonding sites for Pb2+/halide surface undercoordination passivation.
A3. Target geometry: ZnO / UiO-66-X thickness 5–20 nm (primary window 8–15 nm), with controlled missing-linker defects to increase accessible pore volume while maintaining film integrity.

B. MOF-on-ZnO film growth and solvent compatibility (perovskite-processing aware)
B1. Surface anchoring: functionalize ZnO with a thin carboxylate-terminated anchoring layer (e.g., 3-(triethoxysilyl)propyl succinic anhydride hydrolysis → surface –COOH) or direct coordination of linker to Zn sites; confirm by XPS (Zn–O–C signals) and contact-angle change.
B2. MOF thin-film deposition (two compatible routes; choose based on best continuity):
  • Route 1 (preferred): Layer-by-layer (LbL) liquid-phase epitaxy at 60–80 °C using ZrCl4 (or ZrOCl2·8H2O) and 2-aminoterephthalic acid/terephthalic acid derivatives in ethanol/acetic acid modulator, with short cycles to achieve 8–15 nm. Rinse with ethanol only; avoid DMF after ZnO deposition where possible.
  • Route 2 (backup, solvent-minimized): Pre-synthesized UiO-66-X nanoparticles (20–50 nm) assembled into an ultrathin porous film by spin-coating from ethanol and mild pressing/UV-ozone to improve adhesion; thickness controlled by concentration and spin speed.
B3. Perovskite solvent/antisolvent compatibility test (bounded acceptance criteria): expose MOF/ZnO to perovskite precursor solvent (DMF:DMSO) vapor and to antisolvent drip (chlorobenzene or ethyl acetate) in a dummy spin; accept if GIWAXS/XRD shows retained UiO-66 reflections and ellipsometry indicates <10% thickness loss.

C. Mechanochemical APNC loading into UiO-66-X with reproducibility metrics
C1. APNC selection: thiolate-protected Cu-APNCs with known Cu(I)-rich cores (model cluster size 1–2 nm) to bias oxidation toward Cu2O.
C2. Mechanochemical encapsulation (adapted from Asset 1): ball-mill UiO-66-X powder with Cu-APNCs under solvent-minimized conditions (η = 0–0.2 μL mg−1 ethanol), low-energy milling (e.g., 15–25 Hz, 10–20 min, zirconia jar/balls), temperature controlled (<35 °C). Define loading series: 0.5, 1, 3, 5 wt% Cu.
C3. QC and batch reproducibility: quantify Cu loading by ICP-OES (target ±5% relative across batches), verify cluster integrity by UV–vis (cluster fingerprint) pre/post milling and XPS (Cu 2p, Auger).
C4. Formulation for film integration: disperse APNC@UiO-66-X in ethanol with minimal binder (≤0.1 wt% polyvinylpyrrolidone if needed), deposit onto MOF-on-ZnO via spin/spray to create an “infilled” bilayer while keeping total thickness ≤20 nm.

D. Quantitatively controlled Cu+ (Cu2O) formation: oxygen chemical-potential/kinetics mapping
D1. Oxidation platform: a small-volume controlled-atmosphere chamber with mass-flow-controlled O2/N2 and humidity control (dew point), enabling pO2 = 10−4–1 atm and pH2O = 0–30 mbar at 40–100 °C.
D2. Phase-space design (mandatory map): full factorial/DOE sweep:
  • Temperature: 40, 60, 80, 100 °C
  • pO2: 10−3, 10−2, 10−1, 1 atm
  • pH2O: dry (<0.5 mbar), 5 mbar, 15 mbar
  • Time: 2, 10, 30, 120 min
Output: a “Cu oxidation state/process map” identifying conditions yielding dominant Cu+ vs Cu2+.
D3. Definitive Cu2O vs CuO discrimination (not optional):
  • XPS + Auger parameter (Cu LMM) to separate Cu2O from CuO/Cu(OH)2 unambiguously.
  • GIWAXS/GIXRD for Cu2O (111) vs CuO signatures (sensitivity limited; used as supportive).
  • Cross-sectional TEM/EELS for Cu valence mapping within MOF pores (spot checks on selected conditions).
  • Depth-resolved XPS (ARXPS or gentle cluster-ion sputter) to confirm confinement and exclude surface CuO skin.
D4. Self-limiting criterion: define an oxidation “stop condition” as (i) Cu Auger parameter within Cu2O window; (ii) Cu2+ fraction <10% by XPS fitting; (iii) no CuO diffraction; (iv) stable work-function shift over 24 h ambient storage (<20 meV drift).
D5. Batch-to-batch reproducibility: repeat the chosen oxidation condition on ≥5 batches; report mean ± SD for Cu+ fraction, work-function shift, and contact resistance.

E. Device integration with energetics and transport constraints explicitly tested
E1. Device stack: ITO/ZnO/(UiO-66-X ± Cu2O)/perovskite/HTL (NiOx or dopant-optimized spiro-OMeTAD)/Au.
E2. Perovskite: FA/Cs mixed-cation mixed-halide (benchmark composition), deposited identically across all ETL variants.
E3. Controls (mechanism deconvolution):
  • ZnO only
  • ZnO/UiO-66-X (no Cu)
  • ZnO + Cu-APNC (no MOF)
  • ZnO/UiO-66-X with Cu present but unoxidized
  • ZnO/UiO-66-X with forced over-oxidation (CuO-rich condition) to test the reviewer’s failure mode
  • Replace Cu-APNC with inert APNC (e.g., Au25@UiO-66) to isolate confinement/passivation vs p-type energetic effects.

F. Interface-specific energetics + recombination correlation (mandatory linkage to ΔVoc,nonrad)
F1. Band alignment/dipole (operando/angle-resolved):
  • AR-UPS on ZnO/UiO-66-X(Cu2O) before and after perovskite deposition (thin perovskite overlayer series) to track vacuum-level shifts and valence onset.
  • KPFM under illumination and in the dark to map local contact potential difference across grains and interfaces; quantify dipole-induced work-function shift.
F2. Correlation to device nonradiative loss:
  • Suns-Voc to extract ΔVoc,nonrad and ideality factor changes; correlate with measured work-function shift (UPS/KPFM) across the oxidation map.
  • Complement with absolute PLQE/TRPL, but treat Suns-Voc as the primary quantitative recombination metric per critique.

G. Transport/continuity validation (prove “not a blocking layer”)
G1. Cross-sectional conductive AFM (c-AFM): map nanoscale conduction pathways across ZnO/UiO-66-X(Cu2O)/perovskite lamellae; define acceptance as continuous current pathways with no macroscopic insulating gap.
G2. Electron-only devices for contact resistance extraction: ITO/ZnO/interlayer/perovskite/PCBM/Ag (or analogous) to isolate electron extraction; fit J–V/TLM-like patterns and extract specific contact resistance and series resistance. Acceptance criterion: ΔRs ≤ +10% versus ZnO-only while achieving ΔVoc,nonrad improvement.
G3. Impedance spectroscopy: separate transport resistance vs recombination resistance; validate that improvements in recombination resistance are not offset by transport penalties.

H. Direct assays for ZnO basicity/hydroxyl-driven decomposition suppression (interface-specific)
H1. Quantify ZnO surface –OH/basicity before/after interlayer:
  • OH density by O 1s XPS deconvolution and ATR-FTIR of surface hydroxyl bands.
  • CO2-TPD or acid–base indicator adsorption (semi-quantitative) to benchmark basic site density.
H2. Operando interfacial reaction tracking:
  • In situ GIWAXS during thermal soak (65–85 °C) and light exposure to monitor emergence of PbI2 and other decomposition phases for ZnO vs ZnO/UiO-66-X(Cu2O).
  • In situ PL under controlled humidity to quantify degradation kinetics; extract rate constants and compare across stacks.
H3. Ion/hydroxyl blocking evidence:
  • ToF-SIMS depth profiles after aging for I−/Br−/Zn/Cu migration; compare interdiffusion lengths.
  • Bias-stress hysteresis protocol to relate mobile ion accumulation to interlayer choice.

I. Stability testing (ISOS) with mechanistic post-mortems
I1. ISOS-L (MPP, 1 sun, 45–65 °C), ISOS-D (controlled RH), and thermal aging 85 °C (dark) with periodic Suns-Voc and Rs extraction.
I2. Post-mortem: XPS depth profiling for Cu valence drift (Cu+→Cu2+), MOF integrity (Zr signals, linker fragments), and perovskite decomposition markers.

J. Secondary objective to satisfy “water purification membranes” chain (explicit integration)
J1. Membrane fabrication: coat PVDF (or PES) porous supports with a thin UiO-66-X layer (spray/LbL), mechanochemically load Cu-APNCs, then apply the same controlled oxidation condition that yields Cu2O in the PV interface.
J2. Water purification assays:
  • Antibacterial activity (E. coli log reduction) under dark and visible-light conditions (Cu2O photocatalytic contribution).
  • Photocatalytic dye degradation (e.g., methylene blue) and Cu leaching (ICP) to verify confinement and stability.
J3. Cross-validation: use the membrane system to stress-test oxidation stability in aqueous/oxidative environments, feeding back to PV durability claims (chemical robustness of Cu2O@UiO-66).
Feasibility: 1) MOF feasibility is bounded by a concrete, literature-established robust system (UiO-66-X). Zr(IV)-carboxylate MOFs are among the most solvent/oxidant tolerant frameworks, making them defensible under both (i) controlled O2/H2O oxidation and (ii) perovskite processing solvents/antisolvents; acceptance criteria are explicitly defined by GIWAXS/ellipsometry retention tests.

2) Cu+ formation is converted from an underspecified step into a controlled process window by mapping (T, pO2, pH2O, t) with definitive Cu2O vs CuO/Cu(OH)2 discrimination via XPS Auger parameter, supported by GIWAXS and depth/valence mapping (ARXPS, TEM/EELS). A reproducible “stop condition” and batch metrics (≥5 batches) directly address the reviewer’s kinetic/chemical-potential concern.
